term: theology versus grammar of a religious practice
resolution: The raw STMT-COUNCIL-TEACHING-THEOLOGY-NOT-GRAMMAR remains an unattributed mixed reconstruction. New analyst siblings distinguish theological content, a practical role in religious life and normative own-standard endorsement. Descriptive theology can coexist with the original definition-to-own-standard bridge; actual opposition requires an explicit exclusion plus a Defined witness, or actual mixed defined-status witnesses. The alternative relation now uses the exact bridge negation, so merely refuting the descriptive formulation cannot defend the normative bridge. Existing authority/use/neither grammar-fixer cases and their open bridges are unchanged; no theological label selects a case or establishes a source interpretation. Existing Catholic-practice, reference and grammar-case arguments retain normative OwnStandard endorsement and do not classify a move as nonnormative merely because it is theological.
